titulo: Unreal Past, Modal Perfect and Third Conditional
descripcion: Regret in English draws on three structures that learners usually meet in separate units: the unreal past after wish, the modal perfect (could/should/might have), and the third conditional. In real speech they blend into a single train of thought — I wish I'd known; we could have avoided it; if we'd checked, none of this would have happened — and the blending is the actual skill.

filas: if + past perfect, would have + participle

ejemplos.texto: I wish I'd known sooner — we could have avoided the whole mess.
If we'd checked the settings, this wouldn't have happened.
We should have asked; nobody thought to.

notas: These three often appear in sequence within the same paragraph: wish sets the regret, modal perfect names the missed action, the third conditional spells out the alternative.
Would have never appears in the if-clause of a third conditional, even though it's tempting after wish + would.
Could have and might have differ in confidence: could have is a genuine possibility, might have is more tentative.

contraste.es: El español expresa lo mismo con si + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo y condicional compuesto, y el arrepentimiento con ojalá + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo, así que la lógica es paralela. Lo que no transfiere es el modal perfecto inglés como pieza intermedia: el español no tiene un verbo modal separado y lo resuelve todo dentro del propio condicional, así que los hispanohablantes tienden a saltarse could/should have y pasar directo del wish al tercer condicional.

errores: Using would have inside the if-clause of a third conditional.
Skipping the modal perfect and jumping straight from wish to the third conditional, losing the missed-action step.
Confusing could have and might have when the degree of certainty actually matters to the point.

traducciones.de: Ich wünschte, ich hätte es gewusst.

redemittel.expresion: If we'd known, we wouldn't have…

traducciones.es: si lo hubiéramos sabido, no habríamos…
traducciones.de: Wenn wir es gewusst hätten, hätten wir nicht…
traducciones.fr: Si nous l’avions su, nous n’aurions pas…
Avec le recul, nous aurions dû…

autochequeo: Does every if-clause use the past perfect, with no would inside it?
Is the modal perfect present as its own step, not skipped?
Are could have and might have used with the right degree of certainty?
Do the three structures appear in a natural sequence, not isolated?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the regret cluster: unreal past, modal perfect, third conditional. Check every if-clause for would have by mistake, and check whether the three structures work together as a sequence. Do not rewrite the text.
